subject: Pilot terms: cache-first pilot + quantization scope for CloudScribe
messages:
From: Eva Morales <eva@cloudscribe.ai>
To: tessa.morgan@redwood.com
Date: 2025-03-18T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Optimize toolkit pilot — quick context and ask

Hi Tessa,

Thanks for the chat yesterday. Quick context — we're building a writing-assist feature for enterprise customers and expect bursty generation traffic (short prompts, lots of concurrent sessions). We're interested in the Optimize toolkit to get immediate savings on tokens and latency while we pilot.

High-level asks:
- Recommendation on a pilot packaging that balances credits vs. committed spend (we want predictable ops for Q3).
- How batching and KV caching would be configured for a short-session, high-concurrency pattern. Any guardrails we should set?
- Practical guidance on quantization: what to expect for accuracy tradeoffs if we move to an 8-bit or 4-bit profile for certain workloads.

I've attached a crude usage estimate (CloudScribe_MVP_usage_estimates.xlsx) — numbers are knobs, not final. Can you share a ballpark pilot construct and pricing so we can present it internally?

Also looping Jamal (procurement) on this thread.

Thanks,
Eva Morales
Head of Product, CloudScribe
Eva@cloudscribe.ai

Attachment: CloudScribe_MVP_usage_estimates.xlsx (Excel, 27 KB)

From: tessa.morgan@redwood.com

Cc: priyom.das@redwood.com, lauren.bishop@redwood.com
Date: 2025-03-18T11:35:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Optimize toolkit pilot — quick context and ask

Hi Eva / Jamal —

Appreciate the details (and the spreadsheet). Based on the usage shape you provided I recommend a cache-first pilot with focused quantization on non-critical generation paths. Outline below is intentionally conservative so we can tweak after a brief kickoff signal.

Pilot proposal (short):
- Length: 6 weeks (30 business days)
- Credits: 50k token credits + 200k KV-cache lookups included (we can map these to your X sessions baseline)
- Discount: 20% off list for pilot usage, applied to overage beyond credits for the pilot period
- Technical scope: enable prefix/KV caching for session-level prompts (retention window configurable; default 60s for MVP), batching up to 64 concurrent streams with latency SLOs intact, and an opt-in quantization profile (8-bit for gen, 4-bit for embeddings/large-context rerank) with calibration evaluation before rollout
- Ops & observability: per-route token + latency breakdown, and alerts for quality regressions tied to your reference prompt set

Attachments: redwood_optimize_pricing_summary.pdf (high-level pricing tiers & the optimization levers). I'm free for a short sync today or tomorrow to walk through details.

If this looks directionally right I'll align internally on exact credit mapping and a short SOW.

Best,

tessa.morgan@redwood.com

----- Forwarded message -----
From: Eva Morales <eva@cloudscribe.ai>
Date: 2025-03-18 09:12

[see original above]

My notes / ask: please reply inline.

-- Priyom reply (inline / short):
Tessa — I like the 50k/200k split as a starting point. Two pricing tweaks I'd propose:
- Make the pilot credits refundable against first 3 months if they convert to a committed band >= $50k/mo (helps with buying inertia).
- Cap our credit liability by tying KV-cache included lookups to a top-line concurrent session metric (so extremes don't blow budget).

Also: recommend a 15% pilot discount rather than 20% unless legal signs off on refundable credit clause.

-- Lauren reply:
Agree with refundable credits as conversion lever. Also suggest we include an SLA uplift (priority incident triage) during the pilot for one named contact — small ops overhead but materially reduces delivery risk.

-- Karthik reply:
Technical guardrails on quantization:
- Start with 8-bit for generative path; use 4-bit only for embeddings + large context re-ranking where we run batch QA against a small golden set.
- Add an evaluation step: before enabling 4-bit on a route, run a 2000-sample A/B on a holdout to measure rouge/semantic similarity deltas. If delta > 2.5% we fall back to 8-bit.
- Batching config: use dynamic batching with a 15ms max coalescing window for low-latency paths; allow higher coalesce for background rerank jobs.

Can someone draft a short SOW and pilot terms doc I can share with legal/procurement?

From: tessa.morgan@redwood.com
To: Eva Morales <eva@cloudscribe.ai>, Jamal Reed <jamal@cloudscribe.ai>
Cc: priyom.das@redwood.com, lauren.bishop@redwood.com, karthik.iyer@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Pilot terms: cache-first pilot + quantization scope for CloudScribe (updated)

Hi Eva / Jamal —

Thanks for the quick reply. Based on internal alignment here's an updated, actionable pilot offer. I've attached a one-page SOW and the pricing spreadsheet for your procurement team.

Updated pilot terms (actionable):
- Duration: 6 weeks (kickoff target: 2025-04-01)
- Included credits: 50,000 generation-token credits; 200,000 KV-cache lookups (mapped to your concurrent session baseline in the attached estimate)
- Pilot discount: 15% off list on pilot usage; credits are refundable against the first 90 days if CloudScribe signs a minimum 6-month committed band >= $50k/month (refund applies to credits only)
- Overage pricing: pilot-overage billed at pilot rate with 10% buffer capped monthly (we'll provide a projection export)
- Quantization guardrails: enable 8-bit gen by default; we will run a gated evaluation for 4-bit on embeddings/rerank. If the 2k-sample A/B shows >2.5% quality regression we will not enable 4-bit for that route.
- Batching & cache config: dynamic batching (15ms coalescing window for interactive routes); KV cache TTL default 60s configurable to 5m max for sessions where it helps; cache-hit reporting on a per-route basis
- Ops: 1 named priority contact for triage during the pilot + weekly syncs and a final health/metrics review

Next steps:
1) If you accept these terms we can circulate the SOW for signature (attached: SOW_pilot_cloudscribe_v1.docx).
2) Kickoff tech sync to map routes to caching tiers and a short calibration plan for quantization evaluation (aim: 2–3 business days to set up tests).

Let me know if Jamal needs a PO or if you'd prefer DocuSign — we can support either.

Best,
Tessa Morgan
Sr. Strategic Sales Manager | Redwood Inference
